title: Eby Farmstead engagement and 2023 surplus allocation
subtitle: Albert McCormick Community Centre architect, Generation Park sustainability standards, Town Square expropriation, and AMO highway-crossing delegation request.
overview: Council directed staff to start community engagement on the future of live animal displays at the Eby Farmstead in Waterloo Park, ahead of the 2025 Waterloo Park Plan update {{vote:m6}}. Staff expect to report back in early autumn. Residents can weigh in through an online engagement page, surveys and in-park signage.

Council allocated the 2023 property-tax base surplus of $1,865,330 equally across four reserves: tax rate stabilization, capital infrastructure reinvestment, climate action and library expansion {{vote:m7}}. Council also awarded the architectural consulting contract for the Albert McCormick Community Centre renovation and expansion to ward99 architects inc. for $746,629.40 {{vote:m8}}.

Council approved an amending subdivision agreement and a Sustainability Standards Administrative Procedure for Generation Park {{vote:m9}}, and authorized expropriation proceedings for land at the Waterloo Town Square north parking lot {{vote:m10}}. A delegation by-law amendment for Generation Park was passed later with the by-laws. Consent items, including the 2023 investment and development charge reports, were received as information.

decisions.detail: Council approved the staff report and directed a community engagement campaign to gauge public interest in alternatives for the Eby Farmstead operation.
Council approved allocating the $1,865,330 property-tax base surplus roughly equally to four reserves, with audit adjustments split 25% each.
Council awarded RFP24-01 consulting services for the Albert McCormick Community Centre project to ward99 architects inc. for a total of $746,629.40.
Council approved the amending subdivision agreement and the Sustainability Standards Administrative Procedure, and directed staff to bring a delegation by-law amendment forward.
Council authorized the City Solicitor to begin expropriation proceedings for lands at the north parking lot near 45 Erb Street.

debate: On the Eby Farmstead, staff said the farmstead could dominate engagement on the wider park plan, so a focused decision should come first, with a third-party consultant guiding the process.

One councillor asked that the broader park still get a later chance for public comment. Another asked for in-park pop-up sessions. Staff said they want a broad range of park users, not only farmstead visitors.

On dog parks, staff said a leash-free park may have a future in Waterloo Park. They said location should be settled through the park plan, citing the busy area, nearby playground construction this summer, and added traffic and parking.

On the surplus, councillors asked about tax-rate relief. Staff said surpluses are one-time, so ongoing changes need sustainable savings. They noted favourable early assessment growth and a committed efficiency target in the 2025 or 2026 confirmation reports.

One councillor asked the City to lead a joint AMO delegation of municipalities split by provincial highways, to seek updated design guidelines for active transportation crossings. Staff said it would be added to the delegation requests without a motion.
